canonical_bindings.use_in_package: Keeps business meaning, system claims, bridge claims, evidence, confidence, lifecycle, and residue separate.
Shapes Define as a repeatable transform with explicit inputs, actions, roles, gates, outputs, evidence, residue, validation, and boundaries.
Keeps package proposals subordinate to the canonical definition store and its required voices.
Requires every consequential decision to name scope, owner, surface, operation, basis, effect, and challenge route.
Prevents source evidence, schema conformance, or validation from becoming a stronger product, runtime, or authority claim.
Keeps the purpose, desired capability, problem pressure, and change direction traceable while Define discovers and revises the concepts needed to continue.
Routes definition candidates and reusable authority through owner review instead of promoting them by file placement.
Separates a recognized artifact form from whether an instance is authoritative or promoted.
Treats the package as perennial-intent candidate material and questions or run receipts as lifecycle-bound state.
Makes package conformance decidable by shape without confusing shape with truth, ownership, promotion, or execution.

Shapes the exact business-to-DomainSpec handoff boundary while leaving complete ConstructionBinding ownership with the Project and refusing to infer compiler, generated graph, system ontology, implementation, or runtime evidence.

proposals.normative_voice: CyberAlchemy Define is the governed capability that preserves a bounded goal and its originating intent while making the meaning needed to continue explicit. It identifies the required concepts, locates existing definitions, evidence, relationships, and owners, asks when meaning is missing, ambiguous, or conflicting, and gives each concept exactly one current disposition: reuse, specialize, propose, or open. It produces a reviewable Definition Pack for any named consumer and preserves unresolved meaning without choosing the consumer's solution.
proposals.formal_voice: Let g be the bounded result or change sought, i be its attributable intent under CAV2-D39, E be current evidence, C be the declared set of concepts required to interpret g and i, and D = {reuse, specialize, propose, open}. Define yields P = (g, i, E, C, delta, Q, O, R, A), where delta: C -> D is total, Q preserves unresolved questions, O records owner routes, R records typed relationships, and A records authority ceilings. P is admissible only when g remains traceable to i, every c in C has exactly one current delta(c), every support reference resolves or is exposed as a gap, and no output silently replaces i or grants promotion, solution, or execution authority.
proposals.plain_language_voice: Define keeps the goal and the reason behind it visible, finds the concepts the work depends on, checks what the project already means by them, asks about missing meaning, and leaves a reusable record of what is known and what remains open.
proposals.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy v2, Define is a first-class product capability and reusable semantic service, not a mandatory prelude to one lifecycle stage. Its CLI and chat surfaces project the same resumable standalone session. Product work, research, system work, UX, UI, brand work, planning, validation, or another named consumer may use its Definition Pack and may return new questions. Alch declarations, source-linked ontology, Craft, and DomainSpec provide the construction path while CyberAlchemy owns the product meaning and authority boundary.
proposals.boundary: CyberAlchemy Define does not choose product behavior, system structure, experience flow, interface form, brand expression, implementation tasks, or execution. It is not canonical definition promotion, automatic approval, a complete model of human intent, runtime adoption, or external authority. A passing Definition Pack establishes only bounded semantic coverage at its recorded evidence state.

proposals.normative_voice: A Definition Pack is the reviewable output of CyberAlchemy Define that keeps the bounded goal, originating intent, required concept set, one current disposition per concept, candidate or reused definitions, evidence, scopes, owners, typed relationships, unresolved questions, validation state, and authority ceiling together for the next consumer.
proposals.formal_voice: A Definition Pack P is admissible only when P = (g, i, C, delta, K, E, S, O, R, Q, V, A), g remains traceable to intent i, delta is total over C, every reference in K, E, O, and R resolves, Q preserves unresolved meaning, V states validation scope, and A = none unless a separate exact owner decision grants a narrower effect.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A Definition Pack is one checked bundle that shows what every important concept means, what evidence supports it, who owns it, and which questions are still open.
proposals.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy v2, the Definition Pack is a durable semantic input for any named consumer. It keeps the same goal, intent, meaning, and open questions visible in chat, the CLI wizard, and machine-readable artifacts without turning candidate definitions into canon or forcing one next lifecycle stage.
proposals.boundary: A Definition Pack is not the canonical definition registry, a chosen product or system solution, an executable plan, proof that all human intent was captured, or a grant of authority.

proposals.normative_voice: A Define Session is the resumable interaction state for one bounded Define goal. It preserves the current question, prior questions and answers, evidence references, concept dispositions, open gaps, owner routes, validation state, and synchronized CLI and chat projections without inferring answers or consequential authority.
proposals.formal_voice: For one Define goal g, a session state T = (g, q_current, Q_asked, A_given, E, delta_partial, G, O, V, p) where p is lifecycle position. Resume(T) must preserve identity and prior state; a CLI or chat projection may change presentation but not silently change T; any consequential transition requires an authority envelope valid for that effect.
proposals.plain_language_voice: A Define Session remembers the questions, answers, evidence, decisions, and open gaps for one goal so the person can move between CLI and chat without starting over.
proposals.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy v2, the Define Session is the ergonomic center of the interactive wizard. It carries avoidable memory work for the person while keeping human choices, non-answers, evidence, ownership, and authority limits visible.
proposals.boundary: A Define Session is not a chat transcript alone, hidden user-state inference, automatic approval, universal memory, evidence of usability, or authority to promote definitions or execute downstream work.

proposals.normative_voice: A Define Handled Definition Registry is the no-authority collection of semantic handling records created or maintained by CyberAlchemy Define for explicit bounded contexts and intended uses. Each current record binds one concept and context to exactly one disposition, its required payload, sources, decision owner, consumers, and challenge or refresh route without changing any referenced definition's semantic authority or promotion state.
proposals.formal_voice: Let R be a registry of records r = (record_id, concept_id, term, context_id, context, intended_use, current_disposition, disposition_payload, source_refs, decision_owner_route, consumer_refs, challenge_or_refresh_route, current, supersedes_ref, authority_effect). For each (concept_id, context_id), at most one r may be current. Exactly one payload variant corresponding to current_disposition in {reuse, specialize, propose, open} is required. Registry presence, lookup, or validation implies neither semantic promotion nor downstream authority.
proposals.plain_language_voice: The handled-definitions registry records what Define did with each important concept in one exact context—reuse it, narrow it, propose it, or keep it open—without pretending that the registry makes the meaning canonical.
proposals.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy v2, the product owner owns this candidate registry asset and Definitions Governance stewards its record shape. Source or decision owners retain authority over each meaning, the next-use owner decides whether a Definition Pack is suitable, and later runtime storage remains a separate implementation concern.
proposals.boundary: The registry is not the canonical definition store, a definition-promotion mechanism, a conflict resolver, an owner appointment surface, an accepted Definition Pack, a storage-engine implementation, or authority to use a definition downstream.
proposals.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner
